title.zh: 子午面极坐标与矢量逆向投影

summary: Map positive r,theta and polar vector components to meridional rho,Z components.

capability: Map positive polar radius, angle and polar vector components to meridional rho, z and components.
operation: r, theta and polar vector components -> rho, z and meridional vector components
discovery.model: Euclidean meridional coordinate transformation inverse to the forward basis, with theta in radians from +Z toward +rho and no magnetic-field model.
discovery.geometry: Planar signed rho,Z coordinates with positive radius; caller-coherent length and vector units.
discovery.boundary: The origin has no polar vector basis and is rejected; nonzero axis points are valid, and no physical field-null convention is inferred.

identity.relation: rho=r sin(theta); z=r cos(theta); u_rho=u_r sin(theta)+u_theta cos(theta); u_z=u_r cos(theta)-u_theta sin(theta).
identity.definition: Inverse of the same orthogonal meridional basis; theta radians from +Z toward +rho. This explicit inverse fixes the forward convention and preserves vector norm.
identity.model: Euclidean meridional coordinate transformation, no magnetic model.
identity.geometry: Planar signed rho,Z coordinates with positive distance from origin.
identity.coordinates: Caller coherent length/vector units; theta radians.
identity.boundary: Origin has no polar vector basis and rejects; nonzero points on the axis are valid.
assumptions: r>0; no physical field null convention inferred

preconditions: Finite broadcastable real arrays; away from coordinate origin
supported: Axis and signed planar coordinate quadrants

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for nonfinite input or origin; NumPy broadcasting errors propagate.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial tuple on invalid input.

example.description: Transform r=2, theta=0 and polar vector components back to cylindrical meridional coordinates.
example.code:
from scirel.geometry.sampling import transform_to_rhoz

rho, z, radial, axial = transform_to_rhoz(2.0, 0.0, 4.0, 3.0)
assert (rho, z, radial, axial) == (0.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0)
example.expected: The inverse transform returns rho=0, Z=2, rho-component=3, and Z-component=4.

scope: The inverse is asserted to undo the forward basis on four inputs within eight correctly rounded operations per component; a sign error in either vector component breaks the round trip.
The theta=0 case is zero-tolerance exact, because sin(0)=0 and cos(0)=1 are exact.

The inverse's own preconditions are asserted separately from the forward's: non-positive radius and non-finite angle or components raise ValueError, so the two contracts do not share one rejection test.
Test matrix covers the axis case, off-axis round trips, broadcast inputs and both rejection reasons.
Failure matrix gives one executable assertion per rejecting channel and asserts that no partial tuple is returned.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Establishes the inverse relation on the tested inputs only. It does not establish accuracy for large or wrapped angles beyond the sine/cosine parameterisation, and it makes no physical interpretation of the returned components.
known_limitations: Length and vector units remain caller supplied
cannot establish: an independent reference for a non-axis angle; the stated budget is a rounding budget for the composition, not an accuracy claim against an external oracle
